# Lists and task items {#lists}

0.1 shaped lists with `+` continuation lines, `{loose}`, marker columns and task boxes. In 0.2 blank lines and content columns decide the shape: there is no list continuation marker, and a line past the marker column stays in the item (writer, rules of 0.1 that become obsolete). The 18 November ruling D1 lets the first marker fix the style of an ordered list ([#6074](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/pull/6074), C2-B-042).

**U-014** <Badge type="tip" text="rewrite" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> `+` line before a block in an item

::: compare no-render
```text
- step one
+
> a note
- step two
```
```crv
- step one

  > a note
- step two
```
:::

**U-015** <Badge type="danger" text="report" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> `+` line before a paragraph in an item
Tool: Review by hand: `- a`, a blank line, `  second`, `- b` keeps `second` in the item, but as `<p>second</p>` where 0.1 wrote it bare (C2-H-034, U-019).

::: compare no-render
```text
- a
+
second
- b
```
```crv
- a

  second
- b
```
:::

**U-133** <Badge type="danger" text="report" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> Under C2-H-032, `- [ ] +` writes a task item with an unlabeled checkbox and no item class or generated style. For `-{#k} [x] bare` followed by `  # inside`, 0.1 uses `aria-label="bare"`.
Tool: Review task HTML.

::: compare no-render
```text
- [ ] +
```
```text
<ul class="task-list">
  <li class="task" style="list-style: none"><input type="checkbox" disabled aria-label="+"> +</li>
</ul> A following heading can also extend the checkbox aria label to include heading text.
```
:::

**U-444** <Badge type="danger" text="report" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> The first paragraph of a tight item or of a one-block description that holds only images, `- ![a](a.png)` ⏎ `  ![b](b.png)` ⏎ `- c`, or `: ![a](a.png) ![b](b.png)` below a term; or the first paragraph of a tight item that a bare block image follows, `- a` ⏎ `+` ⏎ `![x](i.png)` ⏎ `- b`, which U-014 rewrites to a blank line
Tool: Review by hand: no 0.2 source writes the paragraph bare, so a style or script that expects the `<img>` directly in `<li>` or `<dd>` finds a `<p>` around it.

::: compare no-render
```text
- ![a](a.png)
  ![b](b.png)
- c
```
```text
<ul>
  <li><p><img src="a.png" alt="a">
<img src="b.png" alt="b"></p></li>
  <li>c</li>
</ul> A paragraph that C2-H-034 writes bare as the first block of a tight list item, or C2-H-040 as the one visible block of a description, keeps its <p> when its bare form would not import as that one paragraph (C2-H-018, #6832): its content is only images, whitespace and comments, which would import as one image paragraph per <img> (Exception C2-M-013), or a bare block image of the same item follows it and would join its run (C2-M-012). 0.1 wrote such a paragraph bare: <li><img src="a.png" alt="a">
<img src="b.png" alt="b"></li>. The second shape comes from a `+` line before a block image, `- a`, `+`, `![x](i.png)`, `- b`, which U-014 rewrites to a blank line: 0.2 writes <li><p>a</p> and the bare <img>, 0.1 <li>a and the bare <img>. No 0.2 source writes the paragraph bare. The source stays; the tool compares the 0.1 HTML with the <p> added at these paragraphs only and reports each one. A first paragraph with text and no following block image stays bare in both.
```
:::
